findings.key_quote: Operating income increased from $19.2 billion in Q2 2025 to $27.5 billion in Q2 2026
findings.justification: This evidence shows operating income increased from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, which demonstrates improving profitability. However, it does not address whether there was an offsetting rise in operating costs. The claim requires both improving profitability AND no offsetting rise in operating costs to be fully decided.

findings.key_quote: Three Months Ended June 30, 2025 2026 Operating Expenses: Cost of sales $ 80,809 $ 95,778 Fulfillment 25,976 29,633 Technology and infrastructure 27,166 33,158
findings.justification: This evidence shows that total operating expenses increased from $148,531 million in Q2 2025 to $173,145 million in Q2 2026 for the three months ended June 30. The table shows increases across all major operating expense categories (cost of sales up 19%, fulfillment up 14%, technology and infrastructure up 22%). This contradicts the claim that profitability improved 'without an offsetting rise in operating costs' - operating costs clearly rose.

This derived metric shows operating margin increased from 11.4% in Q2 2025 to 13.7% in Q2 2026, which supports improving profitability. However, an improving margin percentage does not decide whether there was an offsetting rise in absolute operating costs - margins can improve even when costs rise if revenue rises faster.

findings.key_quote: The increase in North America operating income in Q2 2026 and for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the comparable prior year periods, is primarily due to increased unit sales and increased advertising sales, partially offset by increased shipping, fulfillment, and technology and infrastructure costs.
findings.justification: This passage states that operating income increased but was 'partially offset by increased shipping, fulfillment, and technology and infrastructure costs' for Q2 2026. This indicates there were increases in operating costs, which is relevant context but the passage covers both Q2 and six months periods without clearly isolating Q2 2026 figures.

findings.key_quote: The increase in AWS operating income in Q2 2026 and for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the comparable prior year periods, is primarily due to increased sales, partially offset by spending on technology infrastructure
findings.justification: This passage indicates AWS operating income increased but was partially offset by spending on technology infrastructure for Q2 2026. This provides context about cost increases but does not provide the complete picture needed to decide the overall claim about operating costs.

The evidence shows operating income was $19.171 billion in Q2 2025 and $27.461 billion in Q2 2026, representing an increase of $8.29 billion or 43.2%. This contradicts the assertion that operating income level increase was 'None' - there was clearly a substantial increase.
